title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes

details.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
details.abstract: We are excited to share our paper, SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-Forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes ! SplatAnything is v3 of the InfiniSplat series . We are dedicated to developing high-quality feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction models for autonomous driving, robot navigation, AR/VR, and game development. From everyday objects and human subjects to expansive aerial scenes, SplatAnything transforms simple captures into 3D Gaussian scenes. It also supports Rig-Recon for autonomous driving and Pano-Recon for AR/VR, enabling 3D reconstruction from multi-camera rigs and 360° panoramas. 😋 Give SplatAnything a try! https://huggingface.co/spaces/ritianyu/SplatAnything

title: P^2-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors

details.title: P^2-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors
details.abstract: 🔥 Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) is now a standard way to consolidate domain experts into one model, yet the student still has to climb to every teacher on its own, and some domains are left behind. What if the experts' weights could guide the student, not only their logits? P²-MOPD writes every student module as its own learnable weights plus a weighted sum of the frozen expert task vectors (expert minus base model), and trains the weights and the mixing coefficients α jointly under the same MOPD loss. The experts become parameter priors : one learnable scalar per module moves the student along a whole expert direction, while the student weights remain free to go beyond any merge. The two channels, student weights and coefficients, share one backward pass, α is folded into the weights, and the trained model is a standard checkpoint with no change at inference. Key results (Qwen3-1.7B / 4B; medicine, law, finance, instruction following): Half the steps: P²-MOPD surpasses the final average recovery of MOPD after half the training steps, at ≤0.55× of its wall-clock. Higher final recovery: 94.7% vs 80.9% (1.7B) and 94.9% vs 83.1% (4B). Balanced recovery: worst-domain recovery rises from 32% / 47% to 88% / 89%, and the across-domain std falls from 28 / 22 to about 5. A learned, reproducible mixture: across 3 training seeds the mean coefficient of every teacher agrees to within 0.01, and the mixture consistently weights the lagging teacher the most. Why it works: MOPD's gap is one of reachability , not of cross-domain conflict. Student weight-only steps barely move along the task vector of the domain they fail to recover, while P²-MOPD moves 13–15× farther along it through a single scalar per module; random directions in place of the task vectors give no gain, so what matters is the expert direction itself. The coefficients also turn cross-domain interference into a contest over a few interpretable scalars, which the gradient settles in favour of the lagging domain. Neither channel suffices alone: coefficients only (a learned merge) stay far below, weights only (MOPD) leave a domain behind, and the combination (P²-MOPD) gives both the best average and the best worst-domain recovery. In one line: expert weights, not only expert predictions, can supervise distillation. Kept as learnable priors throughout training, they guide where the student moves. 💻 Code: https://github.com/SinuoWang/P2-MOPD We welcome feedback and discussion!

title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis

details.title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
details.abstract: We introduce LongBanana, to our knowledge the first expert-designed and expert-verified benchmark for long-context multi-reference image synthesis in the age of agent-driven image generation. The task requires retrieving dispersed visual evidence, rejecting distractors, binding entities and relations, and composing one coherent final image from multiple references. LongBanana contains 90 carefully designed tasks organized by a 3-by-3 taxonomy; each task includes about 32 reference images, 20 constraints, and 50 evaluation items, yielding 4,670 expert-specified atomic evaluation items in total. Its graph-grounded evaluation design instantiates each task with reference images and an entity-relation graph, then converts node, edge, and whole-graph obligations into checklist items for Content Fidelity, Relational Binding, and Global Constraint Satisfaction. Reviewed expert labels include a 15% double-labeled subset with 89.4% exact agreement and 0.83 quadratic weighted kappa. We further introduce LongBanana-Gen, an agent-harness framework for long-horizon image generation; experiments show that minimal agent harnesses improve over direct generation, while a ReAct-Plan-Exec-Reflect (RPR) workflow yields harness-dependent gains by strengthening evidence grounding and repair. Together, LongBanana provides an auditable testbed for measuring dense visual evidence use and a shared target for developing stronger agent-driven image-generation systems. Code and data are available at the project page: this https URL

title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution

details.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
details.abstract: Does a higher benchmark score really mean an agent is getting better? 🤔 In our paper, we go beyond surface-level benchmark evaluations to investigate what actually happens during agent evolution and why improvements do not always translate into better agents. We systematically study agent evolution from three perspectives, Phenomenology, Generalization, and Mechanisms , and further dissect four key stages: Select, Analyze, Mutate, and Gate . Building on these insights, we introduce EvoAudit and Audit-Guided Evolution (AGE) , moving toward more reliable, evidence-driven agent self-improvement. 💻 Code: https://github.com/simple-agent-lab/RSIHub

title: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models

details.title: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
details.abstract: We are excited to introduce EvoWorld, a video generation framework for out-of-sight world evolution. EvoWorld combines a VLM brain with a visual renderer, enabling off-screen entities to remain active participants in an evolving world. Within a bidirectional autoregressive paradigm, EvoWorld supports event-triggered world evolution, subject and scene revisitation, and out-of-sight dynamics rendering through model reasoning.

title: Fast and Exact Relative-Position Attention via Structure-Aware Kernels

details.title: Fast and Exact Relative-Position Attention via Structure-Aware Kernels
details.abstract: We introduce an exact, FlashAttention-style algorithm for relative-position attention (DeBERTa, Shaw, Transformer-XL, and T5), using structure-aware tiling and atomic-free backward computation. At 8K tokens, it achieves up to 6.4× faster forward and 21× faster backward , with 1.8× end-to-end speedup and 2.4× lower memory in speech transcription. Code coming soon!

title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription

details.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
details.abstract: Excited to share Confucius4-R2T2 , our stable-prefix streaming ASR model designed for real-time applications! Unlike conventional streaming ASR systems that repeatedly revise partial transcripts, R2T2 produces append-only, stable text that downstream systems such as voice agents and simultaneous translators can consume immediately. The key idea is Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) supervision, which enables us to transform a full-context ASR model into a streaming one through post-training, without architectural modifications. Built on Qwen3-ASR-1.7B, R2T2 achieves near-offline recognition accuracy with low emission latency, supports configurable streaming chunk sizes, and demonstrates promising cross-lingual generalization. We've made the model and implementation publicly available: 🤗 Model: https://huggingface.co/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2 💻 GitHub: https://github.com/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2 🎙️ Live demo: https://r2t2.youdao.com/demo We'd love to hear your feedback and see what the community builds with it!

title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation

details.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
details.abstract: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation in terms of visual quality and temporal consistency. However, generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent, which autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene (Draft Video) that provides structure and motion signals to downstream video generators. To support this paradigm, we design a dedicated data pipeline and curate two high-quality datasets, Video-Coder-SFT-6k and Video-Coder-RL-2k, which contain diverse prompts and ground-truth reference videos. We further develop the Video- Coder Harness, a unified interactive environment integrating code execution, 3D scene rendering, and execution feedback for agent training and inference. We then train Video-Coder with SFT fol- lowed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback, which combines execution-based and video-based rewards. Additionally, we design an annealing training strategy that gradually reduces the execution reward over time, allowing the model to rely more on the video reward in the later training stages. Experiments show that Video-Coder achieves significant gains, improving Minimax-H3 by approximately 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0. We hope this work can serve as an open foundation for coding agents in video generation, and we fully open-source our data, models, and code

title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression

details.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
details.abstract: Introducing AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression. Give it a model and a latency and memory constraint for your deployment, and AutoCompress automatically produces a compressed model that meets them. No manual architecture design. How it works: AutoCompress builds cost models through efficient, accurate profiling of the model on the target GPU. A differentiable architecture search then automatically picks an architecture that fits the constraints. Finally, we prune the model to the chosen architecture and distill it to recover accuracy. Results: ✅ We compressed models for three diverse real-world use cases: an on-device game NPC (RTX 5070), a long-context coding agent (RTX 5080), and batched datacenter serving (8×H100). AutoCompress improves average accuracy by +6.6 / +2.4 / +0.6 points over the best baseline available (Minitron), with 2–3.3× fewer architecture-search tokens. ✅ At scale, we compressed Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters while keeping about 95% of its mean benchmark score.

details.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations

Our results show uneven cross-task transfer, substantial variation across independent searches, and more limited gains on the larger model. Feedback and discussion are welcome.

title: PREEN: Exemplar-Based Color Style Transfer with Smartphone Editor Presets

details.title: PREEN: Exemplar-Based Color Style Transfer with Smartphone Editor Presets
details.abstract: We present PREEN (Preset Regression via an Exemplar-based Editor Network), which casts color style transfer as regression onto the 29 parameters of a deterministic image editor. Given a content image and a style reference, PREEN predicts a preset, a vector of editor slider values that is interpretable and editor-consumable, not a raster image. The key obstacle is supervision, since an arbitrary real reference lacks a preset ground truth. We therefore supervise with a style-transfer teacher, whose target looks we invert into the editor's parameter space as pseudo-presets, then pretrain a CLIP-conditioned regressor and refine it with LoRA under an image-level CIELAB loss. On the human-curated PST50 benchmark, PREEN applies the reference's color while preserving structural fidelity, leading the baselines on pixel- and perceptual-fidelity metrics. The preset is compact and predicted at sub-second on-device latency. The low-dimensional subspace also exposes a single inference-time strength knob that traces a continuous default-to-vivid trajectory in one forward pass, with every intermediate state a valid editor preset. A two-axis human study shows that raters prefer the vivid end for matching the reference but the default as a standalone photo, a trade-off the knob spans without retraining.

title: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time

details.title: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time
details.abstract: We are excited to share LowRAM, our new KV cache compression method at test-time! LowRAM compresses keys using low-rank factorisation, while small per-head networks predict values from keys. We then keep residual corrections for the hardest-to-reconstruct tokens. This achieves 4× value-cache compression with near-lossless performance. With selective reconstruction, we also reach up to 5× higher peak decode throughput at 4× KV compression on at 262K context! Because LowRAM exploits redundancy between keys and values, it adds a different axis of compression alongside quantisation and eviction. Combining all three lets us push compression to 26.9×, while retaining 94.5% of baseline performance. We see promising applications in long-document QA and serving multiple queries over a shared context, where the predictors can be fitted once and reused. We’d love to hear what you think!

title: Hierarchical Residuals: A Minimalist Decoupling of Residual Width from Compute Width

details.title: Hierarchical Residuals: A Minimalist Decoupling of Residual Width from Compute Width
details.abstract: Residual connections underpin Transformers, but they implicitly tie the residual width carried through depth to the compute width used inside each layer. We introduce Hierarchical Residuals (HiRes), a minimalist architectural change that decouples these dimensions, widening the residual state while keeping per-layer compute width fixed. HiRes groups layers into blocks: standard d-dimensional PreNorm layers operate inside each block, while a wider D-dimensional PostNorm outer residual connects blocks. Learned read/write projections bridge the two spaces at block boundaries, leaving individual Transformer layers unchanged. Across different model sizes and depths, HiRes consistently outperforms vanilla residual addition, with fitted scaling laws indicating a 1.30-fold improvement in FLOPs efficiency. On OLMoE-1B-7B pretraining for 500B tokens, HiRes achieves 0.0208 lower training loss and 1.14-point higher downstream accuracy. HiRes is also competitive with other residual expansion methods such as VWN, mHC and AttnRes with less activation memory and I/O costs. Built from only dense projections and normalizations, it requires neither specialized kernels nor infrastructure-level optimizations. HiRes thus exposes residual width as a practical scaling variable using only standard operators.

title: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting

details.title: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting
details.abstract: 🚀 LLMs Don’t Know What They Know. Can We Trust Their Financial Predictions? Excited to share our latest research: 📄 LLMs Don’t Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for financial forecasting. But when asked to predict the past, are they forecasting—or recalling outcomes they already know? Simply asking the model may not reveal the answer. Common safeguards seem reassuring: trust the vendor’s knowledge cutoff, ask the model whether it knows the outcome, or instruct it to answer as of a historical date. But do these safeguards actually prevent hindsight leakage—or merely change how the model describes its answer? We introduce 🌳 FinDendro , a benchmark of 2,226 dated U.S. financial and macroeconomic facts spanning 1999–2026 , covering macroeconomic indicators, month-end stock prices, and Federal Reserve decisions. 🔍 Key findings: GPT-5 answers 76% of controlled facts correctly but claims to know only 38% . It correctly answers 61% of the facts it says it does not know. Knowledge claims can extend up to seven quarters beyond the measured knowledge boundary. Historical-date instructions remove most claims of prior knowledge while leaving accuracy unchanged. 💡 Reliable backtesting requires measuring what a model knows—not just trusting what it says. FinDendro provides a behavioral procedure for identifying temporal knowledge boundaries and selecting backtest periods based on demonstrated factual knowledge. 📄 Read the paper We’d love to hear your thoughts, especially if you work on LLM evaluation, forecasting, or financial AI!

title: Learning to evolve by matching velocities

details.title: Learning to evolve by matching velocities
details.abstract: Can simulation be avoided when learning neural ODE surrogates of dynamical systems? We introduce Velocity Matching (VM), a simulation-free training objective with guarantees on the learned trajectories. Neural ODEs are usually trained on trajectories: rollouts backprop through the solver, teacher forcing predicts one step ahead. VM stochastically collocates the field along the piecewise-linear interpolant, regressing it onto finite-diffence velocities. Simulation is not only expensive, it also yields degenerate loss landscapes as the horizon T grows. Already for a scalar linear ODE in continuous time, gradients vanish or explode exponentially in T and the minimum sharpens, hindering convergence of gradient descent. Once the numerical scheme enters the loss, long rollouts in the linear case yield a loss that collapses within the scheme’s absolute stability region and explodes outside it. In the nonlinear setting, this translates into a spectral constraint on the learned Jacobian. We motivate velocity-based learning by building a theoretical framework based on stability estimates that bound trajectory error by velocity error along true trajectories, so no simulation is needed. It also yields continuous-time universal approximation results. To this mean, we introduce Velocity Matching (VM), an objective which stochastically collocates the learned vector field along the piecewise-linear interpolant of the observed trajectories, relying on a perturbation in the direction of the first order finite-difference velocity estimate. Experimentally, on nonlinear ODEs test cases, VM reaches lower trajectory error than teacher forcing (TF) and rollouts at the training cost of TF (w/ explicit Euler), and velocity and Jacobian errors drop accordingly (this comes from an implicit regularization effect, explained below). Moreover, VM-learned fields hold a continuous-time approximation property (which we prove via universal approx), namely they can be integrated on finer time grids and with RK schemes other than the training one, whereas rollout-trained models overfit both (here, explicit Euler). On semi-discretized PDEs, rollout training often becomes unstable. With the same architecture and hyperparameters, VM trains stably and attains the lowest test errors, shown here on the Burgers and Korteweg–de Vries equations. Interpolation-based identification goes back to Bellman in the ’70s (structural system identification), and the same reading connects VM to recent Flow Matching approaches. Recently, CFOs have bridged Neural Operators and Stochastic Interpolants, relying on higher-order splines. Although VM relies on a simpler mechanism, this motivated us to study the role of stochastic collocation along the interpolant, and the perturbation it induces. We identify three mechanisms behind its effectiveness: The VM objective is a second-order approximation of the velocity risk, with a consistent minimizer, whereas teacher forcing is only first-order. The VM residual coincides with that of an A-stable implicit Runge–Kutta scheme, but without requiring any implicit solve during training. VM implicitly performs a form of Jacobian matching, which proves critical for learning chaotic dynamics and connects to our universal approximation result in Sobolev norms. As with simulation-based/simulation-free training in flow-based generative modeling, an analogous duality holds for learning dynamical systems. We hope VM and the accompanying theory are a step towards understanding why this is the case.

title: OneTrans-GSR: A Generative Slate Ranking Paradigm Unifying Reranking and Mix-Ranking with One Autoregressive Transformer

details.title: OneTrans-GSR: A Generative Slate Ranking Paradigm Unifying Reranking and Mix-Ranking with One Autoregressive Transformer
details.abstract: We are pleased to share our work, OneTrans-GSR! Paper page: https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.04720 arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04720 In this paper, we explore generative slate ranking for industrial recommender systems and propose OneTrans-GSR, a single autoregressive policy trained with slate-level reward modeling and reinforcement learning, to unify reranking and mix-ranking while replacing expert-engineered cascades. Our key findings and contributions include: A single policy directly generates the final heterogeneous slate under explicit business constraints. Slate-Level Reward Modeling and GMR-PO turn slate generation into a scalable learning problem. Production A/B tests achieve +2.63% GMV/u, +2.06% advertiser value, +2.03% repurchase rate, and −13% serving latency. We hope this work will be useful to the research community, and we welcome any questions, feedback, and discussions!

title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks

details.title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
details.abstract: How can AI agents reliably solve real-world tasks end to end? We introduce Agent-Native Primitives, reusable building blocks that equip tools, code, knowledge, and other resources with their own LLM-powered experts. Building on this idea, HEELO dynamically composes task-specific agent harnesses from eight families of primitives. Across 20+ benchmarks and 46 real-world tasks, HEELO substantially improves agent performance. On our real-world tasks, connecting existing agent systems to HEELO increases completed tasks from 9 to 39 for Claude Code and from 9 to 35 for Codex.

title: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model

details.title: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model
details.abstract: Author here. Can a small model be proven exact at arithmetic on inputs of every length? 🧮 The theory If each step of a model reads only a bounded view of an external memory, exactness at all lengths reduces to exactness on a finite set of views . Proved in Lean, along with: Necessity: once steps can also read earlier steps, no finite test suffices . Robustness: the guarantee survives bounded numerical error. Composition: certified procedures stay certified when combined. ⚙️ In practice Qwen3.5-0.8B + a small adapter passes all 2,446 views on a laptop GPU, in the browser. It is certified for + − × ÷ √ gcd at any length. 220 pre-registered problems Score Sketchpad (0.8B) 220 GPT-6.1 Sol · Claude Opus 5.5 · Gemini 4 Argon 217 · 216 · 207 Five open-weight models 149–199 Qwen3.5-27B · Qwen3.5-0.8B (base) 121 · 23 On 1,000-digit sums : Sketchpad 20/20; frontier models 19, 17, 9; every open-weight model ≤ 2. 🔗 Live demo · Code

title: Human-Centred, Risk-Constrained Evaluation of Financial Document Recognition: Evidence, Critical Errors, and Selective Automation

details.title: Human-Centred, Risk-Constrained Evaluation of Financial Document Recognition: Evidence, Critical Errors, and Selective Automation
details.abstract: How should we evaluate whether an AI system can be trusted to read financial documents and not merely transcribe them? Conventional OCR metrics such as character and word error rates capture transcription quality, but they can overlook something fundamental: a seemingly minor recognition error can alter a financial amount, reverse the meaning of a transaction, or compromise the reliability of an extracted financial fact. This work argues that financial document recognition demands a fundamentally different evaluation perspective: one that measures not only what a system recognizes, but also whether the resulting financial information is correct, structurally consistent, evidence-grounded, and safe to rely upon. I develop a human-centred, risk-aware evaluation framework that brings together financial fact correctness, evidence grounding, critical-error acceptance criteria, uncertainty estimation, and risk–coverage analysis for selective automation. The broader contribution is a shift from measuring how accurately AI reads financial documents to evaluating how reliably its outputs can support consequential financial workflows. The central question is not simply whether an AI system can read a financial document, but whether we have sufficient evidence to trust what it says it has read. I welcome feedback, critical discussion, and perspectives from researchers working on document intelligence, OCR, and trustworthy AI.

title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters

details.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
details.abstract: 🤔 Post-training usually gives you one policy for one fixed weighting of objectives, but different users and settings call for different trade-offs. 🎛️  We introduce LambdaMix, a parameter-efficient method that learns a whole family of preference-conditioned policies with group-relative online RL. 🧩 LambdaMix trains one low-rank adapter per objective together on a frozen base model. A single preference vector does two things: it picks the adapter mixture that generates responses, and it weights the separately normalized rewards used to update the adapters. 🔁 After one training run, you can change preferences at inference with no further optimization. We test LambdaMix across four base LLMs: 🛡️ on helpfulness vs. harmlessness 🧮 on math with instruction following 🕵️ on rewriting comments while removing clues about personal attributes 📈 LambdaMix achieves higher hypervolume than all evaluated conditioned and policy-merging baselines. ⚡ It also uses fewer training completions and less adapter storage than a set of GRPO specialists. 💻  Code: https://github.com/ckarouzos/lambdamix

title: Knowing When to Teach: Learning from Teachable Prefixes in Multilingual Reasoning Distillation

details.title: Knowing When to Teach: Learning from Teachable Prefixes in Multilingual Reasoning Distillation
details.abstract: Even when a teacher model has the reference solution, it can start following a student’s mistakes as they accumulate. We call this Teacher Drift, and we find that it tends to happen earlier in lower-resource languages. Our method, TOPSD, selects a prefix of the student’s reasoning and uses it for training only if the teacher can still reach the correct answer from that point. Across 10 languages and three model sizes, TOPSD consistently improves on standard on-policy self-distillation, with the largest gains in low- and medium-resource languages.

title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding

details.title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding
details.abstract: Can we trust a protein design just because its predicted structure looks correct? In our NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations & Datasets paper, we show why static motif-scaffolding benchmarks tell only part of the story. Of 55 statically successful design–problem pairs, only 31 passed our molecular dynamics validation criteria, and just 8 passed every check. We introduce BILBY, two complementary open research resources: 🧬 BILBY-PRO: 220 systematically derived functional motif-scaffolding benchmarks from PROSITE-linked experimental structures. 🔬 BILBY-MD: A reusable molecular dynamics framework for assessing structural drift, motif-contact preservation, and conformational ensemble fidelity against experimental references. Our MD study evaluates designs from the original MotifBench benchmark, independently of the new BILBY-PRO dataset. We hope BILBY will help make evaluation of generative protein-design methods more rigorous, reproducible, and physically meaningful. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07723 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/HFMI-PROFOUND/BILBY-PRO MD framework: https://github.com/PROFOUND-HFMI/BILBY-MD Feedback and discussions are very welcome!
